title: Unit – 5 : Session – 4 : SLO – 2  |  Topological Sorting in a DAG
sections: I. Fill in the Blanks
Topological sorting is only possible for DIRECTED ACYCLIC GRAPHS (DAGs).
In topological sorting, the PREDECESSORS (dependencies) of each vertex appears before the vertex itself.
The time complexity of topological sorting using DFS is O(V + E).
In topological sort, if a graph contains a cycle, the sort is IMPOSSIBLE (not possible).
DFS-BASED method and KAHN'S ALGORITHM (BFS/in-degree based) are two standard methods for topological sorting.
II. True or False
Topological sorting applies to both directed and undirected graphs — FALSE (directed acyclic graphs only).
A topological sort can have multiple valid orderings for the same graph — TRUE.
In a topological sort, all outgoing edges from a vertex are considered before visiting it — FALSE
(all INCOMING dependencies must be resolved first).
Topological sorting is useful for scheduling tasks based on dependencies — TRUE.
III. Short Answer Questions
Topological sorting: a linear ordering of the vertices of a DAG such that for every directed edge u -> v,
vertex u comes before v in the ordering.
Applications: course prerequisite scheduling; build systems / task dependency resolution (e.g. Makefile),
also package installation ordering.
Cyclic graph: NO — a cycle means each vertex in the cycle depends on another, so no vertex can come first;
a topological order exists if and only if the graph is acyclic.
IV. Complete the Missing Parts (DFS-based Topological Sort)
1. Mark all vertices as UNVISITED
2. For each unvisited vertex: a. Call the TOPOLOGICAL SORT (DFS utility) function
3. In the recursive function:
a. Mark the vertex as VISITED
b. Recursively call for all its unvisited ADJACENT VERTICES (neighbours)
c. Push the vertex onto the STACK after visiting all its neighbours
(Finally, pop the stack to get the topological order.)
Two valid topological orders:
Vertex that must always appear before vertex 0: VERTEX 1 (its only direct predecessor; 1 -> 0).
VI. Spot the Error
Incorrect: 'a vertex is placed before all its incoming edges.'
Correct: In a topological sort, a vertex is placed AFTER all vertices that have edges coming INTO it
(i.e. all its predecessors/dependencies appear before the vertex); equivalently, for every edge
u -> v, u appears before v.
VII. Challenge Question
A straight chain 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> ... -> n has exactly 1 valid topological order: 1, 2, 3, ..., n.
Every vertex's position is forced by its single dependency chain.
